newsitem.title: BRAZIL: AirTouch expects legal fight over B Band.
newsitem.headline: AirTouch expects legal fight over B Band.

text.p: The Avantel group bidding to run Brazil's Band services expects the privatization to be fraught with legal squabbles but is committed to seeing the bidding process to the end, a member of the consortium said.
Ron Boring, vice president of U.S. operator AirTouch Communications Inc unit AirTouch International, said he was extremely satisfied with the bidding process so far.
The Avantel group qualified in eight of the 10 areas up for grabs, he said.
"The ministry wants to go fast. I think (it) would like to cut through any legal disputes quickly but I would be surprised if there were not a legal battle," Boring told reporters.
Boring added that he was "happy" with the bidding process so far and was not surprised that five consortia had not qualified.
"What surprised me more was that four others did qualify," he said, declining to name those groups.
Consorcio Avantel Comunicacoes Pessoais is made up of Brazilian construction giants Odebrecht ODE_p.SA and Camargo Communications.
It qualified for bidding on areas one through six, as well as nine and 10.
Boring noted the consortium was one of the largest and most experienced operators among the bidders and hoped to win one of the larger concession areas, covering the country's most populous regions.
"The (smaller) B regions look good too," he added.
He said the minimum prices set for concession areas were high but, while declining to reveal figures, added that Avantel had not bid "irrationally."
